data.name: Phileor
data.gender_notes: Phileor is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'philos' meaning 'love' and 'oros' meaning 'mountain'. In the New Testament, Philemon is the name of a bishop or an early Christian. Phileor may be given to a boy as a reminder to be a loving and compassionate leader, or a devotee of the Christian faith. The name Phileor carries the meaning “Lover of” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek. Parents who choose Phileor usually hope their child will grow to embody lover of and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of love and devotion to God

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Phileor total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_hebrew.name: פילאור
in_hebrew.meaning: אהבתו של אלוהים, ידיד של אלוהים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: פילאור הוא שם המשלב שני שורשים עבריים: 'פיל' שפירושו אהבה או ידידות, ו'אור' שפירושו אור או האור של אלוהים. השם מבטא את הרעיון של אהבתו של אלוהים או של ידיד של אלוהים, ומשוייך לתכונות של חיבה, אהבה וקרבה לאלוהים.

in_greek.name: Φιλέορ
in_greek.meaning: Φίλος του Θεού, αγάπη του Θεού
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Φιλέορ είναι ένα όνομα που προέρχεται από δύο ελληνικές ρίζες: 'φίλος' που σημαίνει φίλος ή αγάπη και 'Θεός' που σημαίνει Θεός. Το όνομα εκφράζει την ιδέα του φίλου του Θεού ή της αγάπης του Θεού, και συνδέεται με τις ιδιότητες της στοργής, της αγάπης και της εγγύτητας με τον Θεό.

in_latin.name: Phileor
in_latin.long_meaning: Phileor est nomen quod componitur ex duabus radicibus Latinis: 'amare' quod significat amare vel amor, et 'Deus' quod significat Deum. Nomen significat amorem Dei vel amicum Dei, et coniungitur cum proprietatibus caritatis, amoris et familiaritatis cum Deo.

historical_references.reference: Philemon was a wealthy Christian slave owner in Colossae, Phrygia, who is the namesake of the Epistle of Paul to Philemon. He may have harbored Paul when the latter was a fugitive, and Philemon and his wife Apphia were also part of Paul's traveling ministry.

Phileas of Thmuis was a prominent Christian bishop in Egypt during the period of the Roman Empire. He is remembered for his charitable works and his role in the Council of Chalcedon, which established the orthodox Christian doctrine of the divinity of Christ.
